name: Mac stays usable
ownerWords:
look it's you and ops guys responsibility that this machine is usable.

you -harness side of bullshit, ops guy -app side of bullshit fixing monitoring

setup a 60min cadence duty
goal: The harness side keeps the Mac usable every minute: Prime workers hold no more memory footprint than the working turns and live chats need (0.52 GB a working turn, 0.33 GB a live chat), no working session sits quiet over 30 min, and no queued turn waits over 706 s. Swap and memory pressure are ops guy's to watch; this duty only reads them as context.

metrics.label: Share of the last hour's minutes on the harness target
Share of the last 24 hours' minutes on the harness target
Minutes in the last hour with Prime workers over their footprint budget
Minutes in the last hour with a working session quiet over 30 min
Minutes in the last hour with a queued turn waiting over 706 s
Longest run of minutes off target in the last hour
Prime worker footprint over its budget at the last minute

onMiss: Start one fix job for the top miss with await rlm.create_session(brief, name=..., cwd="/Users/sieunpark/Documents/Github/sieun-pi"), or message the job an earlier run started on the same part if it still works. The brief names the part, its minutes off target, the chat trees behind it and the now numbers, and asks for a root fix in the harness with a test and a commit. Footprint: find what keeps each top worker's finished or quiet sessions alive. Idle: find why those working sessions went quiet. Queue: find what holds the slots. Never kill a session mid-turn, restart the Prime daemon or the :5182 service, or message another chat. An alert flag: tell the chat in one line with the part, the minutes and the tree. All on target: end the turn with no message.
